The record book of acquisitions, each animal's tag or microchip number, written description of each dog, and clear
photographs was unavailable for review. The records of acquisition, identification numbers, full descriptions and clear
photographs are important to maintain to ensure accurate information per animal is available at this facility.
A class "C'' exhibitor shall identify all live dogs and cats under his or her control or on his or her premises, whether held,
purchased, or otherwise acquired:
(c)(2)(ii) A record book containing each animal's tag number, a written description of each animal, the data required by §
2.75(a), and a clear photograph of each animal;
Facility should maintain and make their record book available during inspections so that the records and photos match the
animals that are present.
TO BE CORRECTED BY: JULY 1, 2026

A record of acquisition was unavailable for a new wolf hybrid named "Tawny". This dog arrived in August 2025 but there is
no record of where it was acquired from nor was there a full name and address. Exhibitors are required to make and
maintain acquisition records that fully and correctly disclose information pertaining to acquired dogs.
Facility must provide and maintain a record with the correct information pertaining to the acquisition of "Tawny".
Each dealer, other than operators of auction sales and brokers to whom animals are consigned, and each exhibitor shall
make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose the following information concerning each
dog or cat purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, or otherwise in his or her possession or under his or her
control, or which is transported, euthanized, sold, or otherwise disposed of by that dealer or exhibitor.
TO BE CORRECTED BY: JULY 1, 2026

There is a wooden stockade fence that runs along the primary enclosure fence, of the garage pen, across from primary
enclosure fence of the middle pen. This fence is inside of the walkway between these two enclosures. It serves as a
visual barrier between the dogs that are housed across from each other. There are at least four sections that have broken
and missing pickets, and rotted, horizontal support beams. These damaged areas leave this fence in disrepair.
This fence should be repaired to maintain the structural strength and integrity.
Housing facilities for dogs and cats must be designed and constructed so that they are structurally sound. They must be
kept in good repair, and they must protect the animals from injury, contain the animals securely, and restrict other animals
from entering.
TO BE CORRECTED BY: SEPTEMBER 1, 2026
This inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the facility representatives.
